[LTIM.2.7.3] **A window may not outlast the facts it reads.** A window sees a
fact only while the fact is in working memory ([LTIM.2.7.1]), so it sees no fact
older than the longest any fact of its schema can live. A window longer than
that states a past the engine does not hold. The compiler **must** refuse it with
`DS_VALIDATE_WITHIN_EXCEEDS_TTL`:

- a pattern's `within`, positive or negated, whose duration exceeds its schema's
  TTL ([LGRA.5.2]);
- a `then` step's `within` whose duration exceeds the TTL of the step before it
  ([LTHE.2.3.1]), whose fact must still be live when the step's fact arrives.

A window equal to the TTL is not refused. A schema of another lifecycle has no
TTL and bounds no window. Where `dynamic_ttl` is on, `retain:` may give a fact any
lifetime ([LDTL.4.1]), so no window is refused under this clause.
